info.title: Kiwipow Server for the KiwiPow IDE
info.description: Every call but the sign-in and pairing routes and the engine's own request routes carries the IDE's token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The routes that hand out a token also need the `X-Kiwipow-Ide-Key` header. A refusal answers with a JSON body whose `reason` names it.

get.summary: Not found both when the caller reaches no such product and when the product has no store of its own.

Every user of the tenant sees every shared store - a store is working material, not tenant configuration, so nothing here narrows the list the way "Products I reach" narrows products to the caller's own teams. A product's own store is shown under its product instead.
Every local file the product sent into the store: the document it became and the hash (SHA-256 of the UTF-8 text, lower-case hex) of what was last sent, for the IDE to compare with its file now.
The store's documents, named - what the doc-stores page lists under each store.

Readable before it is finished: the document and its whole section tree, including whatever the fill has made so far. Above your clearance is absent: not found, the same answer as the document simply not existing.

artifacts.description: The names of the artifacts the workspace's repository holds.

AnnouncedWorkspace.description: A repository loaded in a workspace of the developer holding the feature. bool AnnouncedWorkspace.OutsideFeature is set when no scenario of the feature reaches the repository.

AnsweredCommentResponse.description: string AnsweredCommentResponse.State is the pull request's state after the answer: open again once the last comment was answered after a push.

ArtifactRef.description: An artifact a repository is tagged with.

name.description: What the artifact is called within its product.

description.description: What the artifact is, in its product's words.

kind.description: What sort of artifact it is, such as an app or a server.

retired.description: Whether the artifact is no longer built.

repositories.description: The repositories holding the artifact, each with its clone address.

modelReviewLevel.description: How far the model goes in reviewing the artifact's pull requests: none, comment, send_back or approve.

ArtifactResponse.description: Repositories are listed with the product's artifacts only.

BeginPairingResponse.description: What the IDE gets back from beginning a pairing: the poll token it polls with, and the code it displays.

BehaviourTextRequest.description: What one behaviour would read instead, as a proposal or a ruling says it.

path.description: The spec file's path below the workspace's specs folder, with /.

title.description: The feature's title; the spec's own `feature:` when left out.

content.description: The spec file's text, front matter included.

artifactIds.description: The product artifacts the sending workspace holds, as writing the spec would name them.

id.description: The id the workspace gave the spec, as writing it would send; the title its own feature holds is then free.

CheckSpecRequest.description: A spec of the workspace to check without writing it.

accepted.description: Whether the spec would be written: no failure and no title another feature holds.

failures.description: Why the spec would be refused for its shape or language.

titleHeldBy.description: The feature already holding the title; null when it is free.

missingDocuments.description: The local documents the spec cites that matched no section, to upload before the spec.

needsAttention.description: The parts whose wording names the code, each with the words that do, which writing would keep as sent and mark as needing attention; empty while the spec would be refused, whose failures then name them.

CheckSpecResponse.description: What writing the spec would answer.

ChoiceFileRequest.description: The side kept in one file of a resolved conflict, and why.

ChoiceResponse.description: `Finding` is "unchecked" until the arbiter has looked, then "fitting", "uncertain" or "conflicting", with its reason in `FindingReason` and the behaviours, standing decisions or rulings it touches in `Touches`. `Escalated` is true for an open choice that waits for the developer's answer: one the arbiter did not find fitting, or has not checked yet. `State` is "open", "kept", "overruled" or "raised"; once answered, `AnsweredAt` and `AnsweredByName` say when and by whom, `Wanted` is the behaviour wanted instead of an overruled choice and `DecisionId` the decision a raised choice led to. `HoldsHandOver` is true for a choice that holds its feature from ready for acceptance: an escalated one, or an overruled one not yet put right.

ClaimFeatureResponse.description: The approved revision the claim builds against.

ConceptResponse.description: What a concept holds, as Kiwipow Server's UI reads it back.

DecisionAnswerResponse.description: Null until the members handling the feedback queue answer the ruling.

DecisionProposalRequest.description: `BehaviourTexts` gives each behaviour its own text; it may be left out for a decision concerning a single behaviour or none, and is required, covering every one, for a decision concerning several. `ClientId` is an id the reporter chose, which a ruling may name the proposal by.

DecisionRulingResponse.description: Null until the decision is ruled on - The developer rules: who, and when.

DefaultDomainFilterResponse.description: The domains the named repositories have served in the product: where a developer's list starts.

DocStoreContents.description: A doc store the product selects, with its directories and the documents the reader is cleared for, by path.

path.description: The document's directories and file name below the store, with /.

headings.description: The headings of the document's sections in the order they stand; a citation names one after #.

DocStoreDocument.description: A document of a doc store.

DocStoreResponse.description: Guid? DocStoreResponse.DefaultClassificationLevelId is A store's default level; Guid? DocStoreResponse.ProductId names the product whose own store it is, null for a store the tenant shares; int DocStoreResponse.DocumentCount is how many documents it holds.

DocumentDetailResponse.description: A document as Importing a Markdown document (or a later read) returns it: its title and source type alongside DocumentResponse's own fields, plus its whole section tree. Guid? DocumentDetailResponse.ClassificationLevelId is A document's classification, null exactly when the tenant has no ladder (No ladder defined).

DocumentMapResponse.description: What reading a document's map comes back with, as the wire carries it.

DocumentMapSectionResponse.description: One section of a document's map: Outline with summaries' own shape - string? DocumentMapSectionResponse.Summary null is exactly Unsummarised in the map, and no block content is carried at all.

DomainFeatureResponse.description: A feature under a domain; HomeDomain names its home when this is not it.

EnginePolicyResponse.description: string? EnginePolicyResponse.EngineImage is the tenant's engine image, null while the tenant has chosen none. string EnginePolicyResponse.Hosting is "saas" when we run the server, with its container runtime and storage already set up, and "on-premises" when the customer runs it and provides those themselves.

oneOf.description: Set on the one poll that collects an approved request.

EngineRequestPoll.description: What an engine learns when it polls its request.

EngineRequestStatus.description: Where an engine's request stands: pending until its person answers, approved or refused once they have, expired once it lapsed unanswered.

pairingId.description: The engine's pairing, named again when it asks to reconnect.

reconnectSecret.description: Named with the pairing when the engine asks to reconnect; a pairing alone is refused.

EngineSignIn.description: What an engine signs in with, and what it names to ask to reconnect once that sign-in has ended.

ticket.description: Passed to the engine at launch; names one request only.

expiresAt.description: After this an engine naming the ticket is refused.

EngineTicket.description: A start ticket: what an engine started by hand is launched with, so its request reaches its person.

machine.description: The machine the engine runs on, shown to the person; at most 100 characters.

ExchangeBrowserSignInResponse.description: The token the IDE signs in with from now on, the same kind a pairing by code hands it.

oneOf.description: The workspaces and the scenario being built, given when the call names an announced workspace.

state.description: The feature's lifecycle state, such as draft, approved, claimed, ready_for_acceptance or accepted.

workspaceId.description: The id the workspace gave the spec the feature was written from; null for a feature not written from one.

sentPath.description: The path below the workspace's specs folder the spec was last sent from; null for a feature not written from a workspace, or sent without a path.

contentHash.description: The SHA-256 of the spec text its workspace last sent, as received (UTF-8 bytes, lower-case hex); null for a feature not written from a workspace. A change made on the server since leaves it as it was.

FeaturePullRequestResponse.description: string FeaturePullRequestResponse.State is open, approved, sent_back, merged or closed. string? FeaturePullRequestResponse.OpenedByName is the developer who held the feature when it opened, null for a pull request opened before that was kept. int FeaturePullRequestResponse.UnansweredComments is how many comments of its review the building agent has not answered. ChoiceResponse[] FeaturePullRequestResponse.Choices are the choices made unattended in the repositories the pull request changes, escalated ones first, with their state and the arbiter's finding.

GitAccessResponse.description: The Git client's username and password: the password admits the one repository and branch until DateTimeOffset GitAccessResponse.ExpiresAt. string? GitAccessResponse.PrivatePlace is set for a private access: the ref prefix every ref it moves starts with.

GiveGitAccessRequest.description: The repository is named by Guid? GiveGitAccessRequest.RepositoryId, or by string? GiveGitAccessRequest.RepositoryName as it stands in its clone address. Guid? GiveGitAccessRequest.FeatureId left out asks for a repository with no feature. string? GiveGitAccessRequest.Branch left out asks to read only. bool GiveGitAccessRequest.Private asks for the person's private place for the branch, where unfinished work and transcripts are kept and may be rewritten.

HandedAnalyzer.description: A chosen version as an engine or a runner is given it: where to fetch it from and the digests the administrator trusted, so the machine needs no settings of its own to find and check it.

HandedDigest.description: The digests of one platform's artifact: of the artifact itself and of its unpacked files.

HandedSetup.description: What an engine is given at each contact: the whole list of trusted, chosen versions.

revisionNumber.description: The approved spec revision the claim builds against.

active.description: Whether it counts against the developer's limit on active features: false once it waits for review or is ready for acceptance.

HeldFeatureState.description: Where a held feature stands in its lifecycle.

id.description: The repository, as Git access is asked for it.

name.description: The repository's name in its clone address.

cloneAddress.description: Where a Git client clones the repository from, on the Git host.

archived.description: Whether the repository is archived: readable, and taking no push.

IdeRefusal.description: What a refusal to the IDE carries: string IdeRefusal.Reason always, as a stable code to act on, and the rest only where that refusal has it to say: string? IdeRefusal.Error a sentence for the person, string? IdeRefusal.HeldBy the developer already holding the feature, string? IdeRefusal.HeldFeature and string? IdeRefusal.Why the feature that keeps the developer at their limit and why the limit exists.

storeId.description: The doc store, which the product has to select.

directoryId.description: The directory the files go below; the store's top when left out.

classificationLevelId.description: The level the documents take, never above the sender's clearance; the store's default when left out.

oneOf.description: How the files are placed below the directory named: as-specified, the default, makes each file's folders its directories; server-suggests lets the server choose each file's directory, reading its folders as a hint.

ImportedDocuments.description: Documents for one doc store; each file's path is relative to the folder the user sends from.

scenario.description: The heading of the scenario the behaviour stands in, as the spec writes it.

behaviour.description: The behaviour's name, the bold lead-in of its line.

edgeCase.description: The edge case's name, only when the test proves an edge case of the behaviour; null when it proves the behaviour.

test.description: The test's name as its test runner reports it.

repository.description: The address the repository the test lives in is cloned from. One the product does not host is kept as sent.

commit.description: The full id of the commit the test passed on; it need not be pushed yet.

ImportedProof.description: A test that passed proving a part of a spec written from a workspace. The part is named the way the spec names it, since the server's ids do not exist yet.

id.description: The id the workspace gave the spec, its `id:` line; the feature keeps it, and sending it again revises a draft.

path.description: The spec file's path below the workspace's specs folder, with /.

title.description: The feature's title; the spec's own `feature:` when left out.

content.description: The spec file's text, front matter included; its `status:` is the state it stood in locally.

domains.description: The names of the domains the spec probably belongs to: only a hint for the planner.

proofs.description: The tests that passed proving an implemented or verified spec.

ImportedSpecFile.description: A spec file of the workspace.

classificationLevelId.description: The level the features take, never above the sender's clearance; the most open when left out.

artifactIds.description: The product artifacts the sending workspace holds, named on every feature and each of its scenarios.

ImportedTechnicalDocuments.description: Documents for the product's technical store, each naming the artifact it covers or none; folders become directories.

ImportFileKind.description: What a file sent in an import is brought in as: a document of a doc store, a document of the product's technical store, or a spec.

result.description: What it became, one of ImportFileResults; null when refused.

reason.description: Why it was refused, as a stable code; null unless refused or waiting for rework.

message.description: The refusal in a sentence for the person.

directory.description: The path of the directory the document stands in, from the store's top with /, empty for the top itself.

featureState.description: The state the feature took: draft, approved, or ready_for_acceptance when every behaviour was proven.

oneOf.description: Why the feature took another state than its spec was sent in.

proofsLeftOut.description: The proofs sent with the spec that were not recorded.

missingDocuments.description: The local documents the spec's dropped citations pointed to, to send before sending the spec again.

domains.description: The domains the feature stands in, its home first.

needsAttention.description: The parts whose wording names the code, kept as sent and marked for someone to bring in line.

failures.description: The parts of the spec's shape a file received for sorting fails.

importStoreFileId.description: The file kept whole in the product's import store.

unchecked.description: Whether the tenant has no planner, so the spec was not checked against the product.

ImportFileOutcome.description: What became of a file, or why it was refused.

ImportFileState.description: Where a file of an import stands: queued, waiting to be processed; processing; failed, for a reason that passes, and waiting for its next attempt; done, see what it became; rework, refused while being processed and waiting for its sender to reshape it with the planner or remove it; refused, on arrival, and never queued.

id.description: The file in the import queue; null for a file refused on arrival or found unchanged, which was never queued.

kind.description: What the file is brought in as.

path.description: The file's local path, with /, as it was sent.

storeId.description: The doc store or technical store a document was sent to; null for a spec.

contentHash.description: The SHA-256 of the file text exactly as received (its UTF-8 bytes, lower-case hex).

attempts.description: How many times processing the file failed for a reason that passes.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed; null unless failed.

oneOf.description: What the file became, or why it was refused; null while it waits.

ImportFileStatus.description: Where a file the IDE sent stands.

oneOf.description: Product documentation for a doc store the product selects.
Documentation of the architecture and the code, for the product's technical store.

ImportRequest.description: The files of one import, each group naming where its files go; a group left out sends nothing.

ImportTarget.description: A product the caller may write a feature on.

InformationChangeResponse.description: What a change carries / What a change points at: an addition, a change or a removal of a concept, an item, a relation or a state, with its target named either by Guid? InformationChangeResponse.TargetId or Guid? InformationChangeResponse.TargetConceptId (an element of the accepted model) or by nesting (InformationChangeResponse[] InformationChangeResponse.Items, InformationChangeResponse[] InformationChangeResponse.Relations, InformationChangeResponse[] InformationChangeResponse.States, under a concept addition this same spec introduces).

NoServerMark.description: The mark that a feature or scenario lives in apps alone, so no server is taken as part of it. bool NoServerMark.Suggested while it is the planner's and no member has accepted it.

waitsFor.description: The predecessors the feature waits for; empty when it can be claimed.

OpenPullRequestRequest.description: Guid[]? OpenPullRequestRequest.DependsOn names pull requests of the same feature that must merge first.

OutsideProof.description: A proof of the scenario in a repository the scenario does not reach.

OutsideTask.description: A task of the scenario in a repository the scenario does not reach.

PendingChangeResponse.description: One of a feature's unaccepted information changes, shown beside the element it targets - never mixed into it (Pending until acceptance).

machine.description: The machine the engine says it runs on: its own claim.

code.description: The code the engine shows where it runs, so the person can tell the request is theirs.

reconnect.description: Whether the engine asks to reconnect a pairing it had, rather than starting from a ticket.

oneOf.description: Where the ticket the engine names was asked for; null for a reconnect.

ticketAskedAt.description: When the ticket the engine names was asked for; null for a reconnect.

expiresAt.description: After this the request lapses and is no longer shown.

PendingEngineRequest.description: An engine waiting for its person to approve or refuse it.

home.description: Whether it is the feature's home domain.

PlacedDomain.description: A domain a written spec's feature stands in.

PollPairingResponse.description: Guid? PollPairingResponse.Token is set only once string PollPairingResponse.Status is "confirmed" - what the IDE then signs in with.

slug.description: How the product is named in its repositories' clone addresses.

ProductResponse.description: bool ProductResponse.IsDemo is Marked as the demo: the one product Task<SetUpDemoResult> DemoProduct.SetUpDemo(Guid tenantId, Guid userId, string userName) scaffolds.

proof.description: The proof as it was sent.

ProofLeftOut.description: A proof the server did not record, and why.

ProofLeftOutReason.description: Why a proof was left out: incomplete, its test, repository or commit is missing; names-nothing-in-the-spec, no standing behaviour or edge case has those names; spec-arrived-as-draft, only an approved spec is built against, so no proof of a draft is kept.

PullRequestStrategyResponse.description: How the IDE shapes its work: string PullRequestStrategyResponse.Layout is one of the pull request layouts, and each pull request keeps to the product's size limit in changed lines. string? PullRequestStrategyResponse.ChosenBy is "team" or "organisation", and null where neither chose, so the IDE can tell a chosen layout from the default.

pollSecret.description: Sent by the engine when it polls; never shown to the person.

machine.description: The machine the engine runs on, shown to the person; at most 100 characters.

ticket.description: The start ticket the engine was launched with.

pairingId.description: The pairing whose sign-in ended, to reconnect.

reconnectSecret.description: The reconnect secret given with the pairing's last token.

RaiseEngineRequest.description: An engine asking to connect names either the start ticket it was launched with, or the pairing whose sign-in ended together with the reconnect secret given with its last token.

ReachedArtifact.description: An artifact a scenario belongs in, with the unarchived repositories holding it; none means it has no repository.

ReportChoiceRequest.description: `Kind` is "settledQuestion", "resolvedConflict" or "judgementCall". `ClientId` is the id the engine chose, so a report sent again is kept once; `MadeAt` is when the session made the choice. `Unattended` says whether the session has nobody there to ask and `OnDeveloperMachine` whether its engine runs straight on the developer's machine. `Open`, `Chosen` and `Why` are plain words, never source code; `Repository` and `Location` name where the choice lives as the engine names them. A resolved conflict gives `Files`.

ReportDecisionRequest.description: What the IDE reports: a title, the behaviours it concerns (none when the spec never mentions the behaviour at hand), and the finding in words - what the code does and where it lives, never the code itself. `ClientId` is an id the reporter chose: a report naming one the feature already has answers that decision and records nothing, and a ruling may name the decision by it.

ReportedProof.description: A proof as the IDE reports it: exactly one of the behaviour and the edge case it proves, the commit the test passed on, and the feature's mark the IDE had received when the work was done.

ReportedTask.description: A task as the IDE reports it: its position on the board is its place in the reported list.

ReportProofsResponse.description: The revision the claim now builds against.

RepositoryAnalysisResponse.description: Whether the repository is analysed, which commit the facts handed out are for, and whether a newer one waits.

ReviewCommentResponse.description: A comment of a review with its answer, null until given. A line comment carries string? ReviewCommentResponse.LineText, the line as it was left on, and bool ReviewCommentResponse.LineChanged when a later push changed that line. string? ReviewCommentResponse.Author is null for the server's own comment; bool ReviewCommentResponse.ByModel marks the model's.

RuleDecisionRequest.description: `Way` is one of "proposal", "keepSpec" or "ownText" - Taking a proposal's three ways to rule. `ProposalId` is read only for "proposal", and names the proposal by its own id or the one its reporter chose; `Text` is read only for "ownText". `Unattended` is set when the session ruling it has nobody there: such a ruling is refused, since only the developer rules. A ruling the developer made themselves leaves it unset.

ScenarioReach.description: What a scenario reaches: the artifacts it belongs in, the unarchived repositories holding them, and the work kept in repositories outside that reach.

SearchHitResponse.description: What a hit says, as the wire carries it.

SearchJudging.description: Whether the decision model judged a search's hits.

SearchRequest.description: A search: Guid? SearchRequest.ProductId or Guid? SearchRequest.StoreId names its scope (Scope named by the search, exactly one of the two), int? SearchRequest.Limit is A capped number of hits' own opt-in for fewer or more than the default. Guid? SearchRequest.DirectoryId or Guid? SearchRequest.DocumentId, at most one of the two, narrows the search within that scope. Guid? SearchRequest.ArtifactId keeps to the documents covering that artifact and those covering the whole product.

SearchReranking.description: Whether a search's ranking was reordered by the installation's reranker.

judging.description: A search whose decision model failed says its hits were not judged.

reranking.description: A search whose reranker failed says its hits were not reranked.

SectionReadResponse.description: What reading a section by id comes back with, as the wire carries it: string SectionReadResponse.Content is Rendered as Markdown, string SectionReadResponse.DocumentTitle and string SectionReadResponse.Place are what a citation is later shown with (docs/product/documents.md#Citations).

SectionResponse.description: One section of a document's tree (Headings build the tree), by its stable id (Every section has a stable id). Null string? SectionResponse.Summary or false bool SectionResponse.HasEmbedding is a section still wanting one (Filled in section by section); string? SectionResponse.SummaryError/string? SectionResponse.EmbeddingError name why, when the last attempt failed (A failed section is marked).

path.description: The file's path below the folder it was uploaded from, as sent.

contentHash.description: The SHA-256 of the UTF-8 text last sent, lower-case hex.

directory.description: The path of the directory the document stands in now, from the store's top with /, empty for the top itself.

SentFile.description: A local file sent before: the document it became and what was last sent from it.

SentFilesResponse.description: Every local file the product sent into a store, for the IDE to tell which of its files changed since.

storeNotice.description: What the agent is told about the store documents; empty when it gets none.

precedence.description: What the agent is told about the rules: its own instructions hold wherever the two contradict.

SessionHouseRules.description: The house rules one agent session gets: none when it works on no product.

SessionInstruction.description: An instruction an agent session follows; a product's takes precedence over the teams'.

SessionSkill.description: A skill offered to an agent session.

SessionStoreDocument.description: A technical store document handed to a session in full.

SpecArtifactResponse.description: An artifact a feature or scenario names; bool SpecArtifactResponse.Suggested while it is the planner's and no member has accepted it.

SpecBehaviourResponse.description: A behaviour is one provable sentence, with its citations and the edge cases under it. bool SpecBehaviourResponse.Removed is Striking what should not be built (see bool SpecScenarioResponse.Removed).

SpecCitationResponse.description: Cited above the reader's clearance: bool SpecCitationResponse.Readable false means string? SpecCitationResponse.DocumentTitle and string? SpecCitationResponse.Place are both null - the citation is still an entry of its behaviour's or edge case's own list, so it never reads as uncited, but names nothing the reader could open.

text.description: The contract in Markdown, the way an agent fitting a spec to it reads it.

SpecContractResponse.description: The contract every spec written to the server is checked against.

SpecEdgeCaseResponse.description: An edge case under its behaviour, with its own citations. bool SpecEdgeCaseResponse.Removed is Striking what should not be built (see bool SpecScenarioResponse.Removed).

detail.description: The part of the spec the failure is about, such as a name used twice; null when it is about the whole spec.

words.description: For names-the-code, the words that name the code, to reword exactly those; null otherwise.

SpecFailure.description: Why a spec was refused: a short reason and the part of the spec it is about.

SpecFailureReason.description: Why a spec was refused. For its shape: no-goal, several-goals, scenario-without-behaviour, unnamed-part, name-used-twice and under-edge-case. For its language: names-the-code. not-a-spec: the file is not a spec, such as the workspace's unfiled-decisions.md or future-work.md. invalid-path and already-taken-in come only from the import of spec files that wait to be taken in.

SpecResponse.description: What a spec holds: a goal, its scenarios in order, its open questions, and its information changes. NoServerMark? SpecResponse.NoServer is set when the feature is marked as living in apps alone, null when it is not.

SpecScenarioResponse.description: A scenario: a stable id, a title, an optional line on the situation, and its behaviours in order. bool SpecScenarioResponse.Removed is Striking what should not be built: a struck scenario is still returned here, marked, rather than being left out. NoServerMark? SpecScenarioResponse.NoServer is the scenario's own mark of living in apps alone.

StandingItemResponse.description: Standing decisions and later work items of a product: the two lists kept apart from the features and the specs. Both share one shape and are told apart by their kind.

StoreFile.description: A local file of the workspace sent into the store, naming the artifact it covers or none.

kind.description: Whether it is an app or a server.

description.description: A sentence on what it is.

StructureArtifact.description: An app or server the product is built as, which an import names for the workspace holding it.

UploadedEntriesResponse.description: Every entry uploaded for the product that the reader sees: all of them with the right to read requests, otherwise their own.

oneOf.description: What the entry proposes: decision, an unfiled decision, proposed as a standing decision of the product; later_work, a piece of future work, proposed as a later work item. An entry without one is refused (invalid-kind).

title.description: The entry's title, one line of at most 80 characters. A title the product was sent before is not filed again.

text.description: The decision, or what is to be done, in one sentence on one line.

affects.description: The names of the features and domains the entry reaches, matched to the product's by name.

UploadedEntry.description: One unfiled decision or piece of future work the IDE sends.

title.description: The entry's title as it was taken; a title matches whatever its letter case.

codeWords.description: The words of the entry as last sent that name the code, marked for triage; empty when none do.

UploadedEntryHeld.description: An entry the IDE uploaded, as the product holds it now.

UploadedEntryResult.description: What became of an uploaded entry: filed, a request now waiting for triage; updated, a request of the same title still open took the new text; already-uploaded, the product holds a request of that title and nothing changed; refused, see the reason.

UploadedEntryState.description: Where an uploaded entry stands: open, waiting for triage; triaged, given an outcome; withdrawn, taken back by its uploader, so the product no longer holds it and uploading it again files it anew.

path.description: The file's path below the folder the user uploads from, with /. As specified, its folders become directories under the directory named; when the server places it, its folders are a hint. A file sent again from the same path becomes a new version of the document it became.

UploadedFile.description: One local file the IDE sends.

UploadEntriesResponse.description: What became of each uploaded entry, answered on its own.

title.description: The entry's title as it was taken.

reason.description: Why a refused entry was refused: invalid-kind, invalid-title (empty, over 80 characters or on several lines) or invalid-text (empty or on several lines). Null unless refused.

WaitingPredecessor.description: A feature that has to be done before another and is not yet.

messages.description: The messages other workspaces left for the calling workspace; each is given once and then gone.

WorkspaceView.description: The workspaces announced on a feature and the scenario being built; null means none is being built. IReadOnlyList<string> WorkspaceView.ScenarioArtifacts are the artifacts the scenario being built belongs in, and IReadOnlyList<string> WorkspaceView.ArtifactsWithoutWorkspace those of it (of the whole feature when none is being built) that no announced workspace holds.

ide-token.description: The token a browser sign-in or a confirmed pairing handed the IDE.

ide-key.description: The key built into the KiwiPow IDE, needed only where a token is handed out.
ide-key.name: X-Kiwipow-Ide-Key
